 Live Game Thread: Mizzou Attempts to Right the Ship Against Arkansas
 The Tigers are in much need of a win coming out of the bye week
 by Colin Simmons Oct 31, 2026, 11:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 What was once a Thanksgiving Turkey Bowl affair has been switched to a showdown on All Hallows’ Eve between No. 23 Missouri Tigers football (5-2, 2-2 SEC) and Arkansas (3-4, 1-3 SEC).
 Since its inception into the SEC, Mizzou holds a 10-2 advantage in the Battle Line Rivalry, currently riding a four-game win streak. The last time the Razorbacks picked up a win in the matchup was 2021 in Fayetteville. They’ll aim for a similar result at home tonight against a team that has struggled coming out of the bye week under head coach Eli Drinkwitz.
 The Tigers were shell-shocked against Ole Miss in Week 7. They now enter as 10-point favorites in a meaningful tune-up game.
 Arkansas is facing different circumstances coming out of its bye week after a 31-21 win over Vanderbilt in Week 7. They also played No. 15 Tennessee to a 24-17 defeat the week prior. KJ Jackson and Chris Marshall enter as a dynamic duo in the passing game, but the Razorback defense is fourth worst in defending the run and second worst in sacks in the conference this season.
 Mizzou gets a boost with Ahmad Hardy and other Tigers listed as active for the matchup.
 We’ll have the most notable updates from the game here in this article as Mizzou looks to bounce back. For all of our live updates, check our forums over at RockM+ .
 Pregame
 Mizzou won the toss and elected to defer to the second half. Arkansas will receive, and the Tigers will defend the north end zone. 
 Final – Mizzou: 34, Arkansas: 10
 First Quarter
 Brunno Reus begins the Battle Line Rivalry by booting the opening kickoff for a touchback. KJ Jackson and the Razorback offense will get the first crack at points. 
 Mizzou’s defense gets Arkansas off the field after allowing one first down. Jackson went 2-for-5 for 20 yards and took one designed run for five yards. It’s clear that the Razorbacks have a lack of faith in the run game. 
 The Tigers’ offense matches Arkansas after getting one first down before punting. Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee got their connection going early with consecutive completions on the first two plays of the drive before a false start by Luke Work stalled the offense. 
 Trajen Greco nabbed his team’s third interception of the season after Chris Graves Jr. tipped Jackson’s pass way up into the air. Great field position inside the Razorbacks’ 40-yard line. 
 Mizzou can’t find the end zone, but Blake Craig gets three points on the board from 31 yards out. The offense now boasts a 46.7% red zone touchdown conversion rate. 
 The weather definitely plays a factor. On a 4th&1 attempt by Arkansas, running back Cam Settles was in the wildcat but bobbled the snap. The ball rolled all the way to the end zone on the rainy playing field, and Darris Smith picked it up. 10-0 Mizzou. 
 Boos rain down in Fayetteville as the Razorbacks go three-and-out. Sterling Webb came up with a run stuff on second down, and Donta Simpson forced a rushed throw on third. 
 Ahmad Hardy took his first carry of the season for no gain from the Tigers’ own 25-yard line. Chip Lindsey went back to him on third and short, where he picked up the first on a 5-yard run. 
 Second Quarter
 Mizzou converts on its first fourth-down attempt of the night. DaMarion Fowlkes took the sweep for six yards. It was his third run of the game, being utilized more than he usually is out of the backfield. 
 The 16-play drive that spilled into the second quarter from the first ended in a made 53-yard field goal by Craig. Good to see that for his confidence, but penalties thwarted the Tigers from making a push into the end zone. 
 Mizzou shuts down Arkansas’ 11-play drive and forces a 52-yard field goal. Max Gilbert’s attempt goes wide left, and boos pour down once more as the Razorbacks remain scoreless. 
 Penalties are beginning to pile up as the first half comes down to its final three minutes. The Tigers are up to five penalties for 45 yards. 
 Arkansas gets on the board after executing a 2-minute drill. Jackson found Antonio Jordan for a 37-yard gain before punching in the touchdown himself from two yards out on the quarterback keeper. The Razorbacks trail 13-7 with 41 seconds for Mizzou to respond before the break. 
 After gaining some steam with consecutive throws for 10+ yards to Donovan Olugbode and Naeshaun Montgomery, Simmons throws four straight incompletions en route to a turnover on downs. 
 Third Quarter
 Mizzou opens the second half strong with a red zone touchdown. Simmons led an 8-play, 75-yard drive capped off with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Olugbode. He found Lee to convert on the drive’s pair of third-down attempts, including a 46-yard pass down the seam, the offense’s longest play of the night. 
 Nic Rodriguez forces the fumble on Jackson. It’s the defense’s third takeaway of the night. Simmons and the offense get the ball in Razorback territory. 
 The Tigers turn turnovers into points with another red zone touchdown. Jamal Roberts took the offense down to the goal line on a 43-yard run before getting fed the rock again for the two-yard touchdown. 
 Arkansas’ ongoing 19-play drive will spill into the fourth quarter. The Razorbacks had two third-down conversions and two fourth-down conversions to keep the drive alive for over nine minutes. They’ll have a decision to make on 4th&13 when they come back from the quarter break. 
 Fourth Quarter
 Gilbert ends the 20-play drive with a successful 32-yard field goal. It’s still a 3-score game with nearly the whole frame to play. 
 Mizzou turned to Jamal Roberts to burn some clock, but then he coughed it up. He took seven rushes for 38 yards before fumbling on the Razorbacks’ 16-yard line. It’s his third fumble of the season and first since the Kansas game. 
 Dante McLellan and Jahlil Florence get the Tigers’ offense back on the field after forcing the fumble on Antonio Jordan. It’s the defense’s fourth takeaway of the night. 
 Mizzou extends the lead to 34-10 after Chip Lindsey employs some trickery to get Roberts open with Simmons rolling out to his left. Roberts only had to get through two defenders for the 10-yard touchdown. It’s his first receiving touchdown of the season. 
 The Tigers produce a goal-line stand that should seal the game. Santana Banner came up with the stop on Jackson on the sneak from inside the 2-yard line before Greco broke up a pass to Courtney Crutchfield on fourth down. 
 Roberts is up to 138 yards on 23 carries and has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards on the season tonight, the first Power Four running back to do so. He’s also only the 22nd running back to do so for the Tigers in a single season.
